title: Room Layout Planner with Drag-Drop Furniture & Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive room layout planner with drag-and-drop furniture placement and particle effects. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Use an orthographic camera looking down (top-down view) at a 10x10 unit room floor.
- The room floor is a plane with a grid texture or wireframe grid overlay (1-unit spacing).
- Walls are represented as thin box geometries along the 4 edges of the room (height 0.3 units visible from top).
- Ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light from above (intensity 0.8).
- Background color: #1a1a2e.

## Furniture System
- Provide a DOM panel (id='furniture-panel') on the left side with 4 furniture buttons: 'Sofa' (2x1 units, color #8B4513), 'Table' (1.5x1.5 units, color #DEB887), 'Bed' (2x1.5 units, color #4169E1), 'Chair' (0.8x0.8 units, color #228B22).
- Each button has class 'furniture-btn' and data-type attribute matching the furniture name lowercase.
- Clicking a furniture button enters placement mode. The next click on the room floor places that furniture item as a BoxGeometry at the snapped grid position (snap to 0.5 unit increments).
- Furniture items can be selected by clicking on them (highlight with yellow emissive). Selected furniture can be dragged to new positions (snapped to grid).
- Press 'R' key to rotate selected furniture 90 degrees clockwise.
- Press 'Delete' or 'Backspace' to remove selected furniture.
- Press 'Ctrl+Z' to undo the last action (place, move, rotate, delete). Support at least 10 undo steps.
- Press 'Ctrl+Y' to redo an undone action.

## Particle Effects
- When furniture is placed, emit 20 particles from the placement position. Particles are small spheres (radius 0.05) with random velocities upward and outward, fading out over 1 second.
- When furniture is deleted, emit 30 red particles that scatter outward.
- Particles have gravity (acceleration downward at 2 units/s^2) and fade opacity from 1 to 0 over their lifetime.
- Track active particle count.

## Collision Detection
- Furniture items cannot overlap. If a drag would cause overlap, snap back to previous valid position.
- Furniture cannot be placed outside room bounds (0 to 10 on both axes).
- Collision uses axis-aligned bounding box checks accounting for rotation.

## HUD/UI
- Display furniture count (id='furniture-count'), total area used as percentage (id='area-used'), and particle count (id='particle-count') in a top-right HUD div (id='hud').
- Display current mode (id='mode-display'): 'idle', 'placing:[type]', 'dragging', 'selected'.
- An 'Export Layout' button (id='export-btn') that logs the layout to console and updates state.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- furnitureCount: number of placed furniture items
- selectedId: id/index of currently selected furniture or null
- mode: current mode string ('idle', 'placing:sofa', 'placing:table', 'placing:bed', 'placing:chair', 'dragging', 'selected')
- furnitureItems: array of objects {id, type, x, z, rotation, width, depth}
- particleCount: number of active particles
- areaUsedPercent: percentage of room area occupied (0-100, 2 decimal precision)
- undoStackSize: number of actions in undo stack
- redoStackSize: number of actions in redo stack
- lastAction: string describing last action ('place', 'move', 'rotate', 'delete', 'undo', 'redo', null)
- collisionOccurred: boolean, true if last attempted move was blocked by collision
- roomBounds: {minX: 0, maxX: 10, minZ: 0, maxZ: 10}
- gridSnap: 0.5
- exportedLayout: null or array of furniture positions after export

Update __3D_STATE__ synchronously after every action.
physics_constraints: Furniture must snap to 0.5-unit grid increments. No overlapping furniture (AABB collision). All furniture must remain within 0-10 room bounds on both axes. Particles experience gravity at 2 units/s^2 downward. Area calculation must be exact: sum of (width*depth) for each item divided by 100 (room area). Undo/redo must perfectly restore previous states including position, rotation, and existence.
